116	class Plane:
117	    """The execution plane: what the model can do to the world, and the record of it."""
118	
119	    def __init__(self, root: Path, hidden: tuple[str, ...] = HIDDEN):
120	        self.root = root.resolve()
121	        self.hidden = hidden
122	        self.listed: list[str] = []
123	        self.read_paths: list[str] = []

126	    def _resolve(self, path: str) -> tuple[Path, str]:
127	        p = (self.root / (path or ".")).resolve()
128	        if p != self.root and self.root not in p.parents:
129	            raise ValueError(f"outside the world: {path}")
130	        rel = p.relative_to(self.root).as_posix() or "."
131	        if rel.split("/", 1)[0] in self.hidden:
132	            raise ValueError(f"not part of the world: {path}")
133	        return p, rel

135	    def list(self, path: str = ".") -> str:
136	        """List one directory of the world: one entry per line as kind, size, path. Path is
137	        relative to the world root; '.' is the root.
138	
139	        Args:
140	            path: The directory to list, relative to the world root.
141	        """
142	        try:
143	            p, rel = self._resolve(path)
144	            if not p.is_dir():
145	                raise ValueError(f"not a directory: {path}")
146	            entries = sorted(p.iterdir(), key=lambda e: (not e.is_dir(), e.name))
147	            if rel == ".":
148	                entries = [e for e in entries if e.name not in self.hidden]
149	            lines = []
150	            for e in entries[:LIST_CAP]:
151	                kind = "link" if e.is_symlink() else "dir" if e.is_dir() else "file"
152	                size = e.lstat().st_size if kind == "file" else 0
153	                lines.append(f"{kind}\t{size}\t{e.relative_to(self.root).as_posix()}")
154	            if len(entries) > LIST_CAP:
155	                lines.append(f"...\t{len(entries) - LIST_CAP} more entries not shown")
156	        except (ValueError, OSError, RuntimeError) as e:  # RuntimeError: a symlink loop
157	            return f"error: {e}"
158	        self.listed.append(rel)
159	        return "\n".join(lines) or "(empty)"

161	    def read(self, path: str, start: int = 1) -> str:
162	        """Read a file of the world as numbered lines, from line `start` (1-based), at most 300
163	        lines or 32000 bytes per call; a truncated read says where to continue.
164	
165	        Args:
166	            path: The file to read, relative to the world root.
167	            start: The first line to read, 1-based.
168	        """
169	        try:
170	            p, rel = self._resolve(path)
171	            if not p.is_file():
172	                raise ValueError(f"not a file: {path}")
173	            start = max(1, int(start))
174	            out: list[str] = []
175	            n = nbytes = 0
176	            with p.open("r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
177	                for i, line in enumerate(f, 1):
178	                    if i < start:
179	                        continue
180	                    size = len(line.encode())
181	                    if n >= READ_LINES_CAP or nbytes + size > READ_BYTES_CAP:
182	                        if n:  # one line per call at least, or a long line dead-ends the read
183	                            out.append(f"...\ttruncated; continue with start={i}")
184	                            break
185	                        cut = line.encode()[:READ_BYTES_CAP].decode("utf-8", "ignore")
186	                        out.append(f"{i}\t{cut} …(line cut at {READ_BYTES_CAP} bytes)")
187	                    else:
188	                        out.append(f"{i}\t{line.rstrip(chr(10))}")
189	                    n += 1
190	                    nbytes += size
191	        except (ValueError, OSError, RuntimeError) as e:  # RuntimeError: a symlink loop
192	            return f"error: {e}"
193	        self.read_paths.append(rel)
194	        self.lines_read += n
195	        return "\n".join(out) or "(empty)"

201	class Wire:
202	    """The raw HTTP record: one line per attempt, request and response, with no secret in it."""
203	
204	    def __init__(self, path: Path, transport: Any = None):
205	        self.path = path
206	        self.attempts = 0
207	        path.touch()
208	        self.client = httpx2.AsyncClient(
209	            transport=transport,
210	            event_hooks={"request": [self.on_request], "response": [self.on_response]},
211	        )
212	
213	    def _write(self, **entry: Any) -> None:
214	        with self.path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
215	            f.write(json.dumps({"t": round(time.time(), 3), **entry}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
216	
217	    def _headers(self, headers: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
218	        """Which headers were sent, never what the secret ones said."""
219	        out = {}
220	        for name, value in headers.items():
221	            name = name.lower()
222	            out[name] = "<redacted>" if name in SECRET_HEADERS else value
223	        return out

225	    async def on_request(self, request: Any) -> None:
226	        """Every attempt the SDK makes, headers and body included; the key is never written."""
227	        self.attempts += 1
228	        try:
229	            body = request.content.decode("utf-8", "replace")
230	        except Exception:  # a streamed body has nothing to record
231	            body = ""
232	        self._write(
233	            dir="request",
234	            method=request.method,
235	            url=str(request.url),
236	            status=None,
237	            headers=self._headers(request.headers),
238	            body=body,
239	        )

247	            method=req.method,

250	            headers=self._headers(response.headers),
